# 6.4 Suffix array and LCP array

Phase 6 (Strings), target rating 1900–2200. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Sorted order of suffixes (`sorted-suffixes`)

Build the order of all suffixes in O(n log n); answer k-th smallest substring or smallest rotation questions.

**Works because:** Suffixes can be compared by doubling: rank by the first 2^k characters, then by pairs of ranks.

### Counting distinct substrings (`distinct-substrings`)

Number of distinct substrings = sum of (suffix length − LCP with the previous suffix in sorted order).

**Works because:** Each new distinct substring is a prefix of a suffix that is longer than its common prefix with the previous suffix.

### Longest repeated or common substring (`common-substring`)

Longest substring occurring twice, or common to two strings, from the maximum adjacent LCP value.

**Works because:** Any two suffixes' longest common prefix is the minimum of adjacent LCP values between them, so the best pair is adjacent.

### Occurrences via the sorted order (`occurrences-by-order`)

Find all occurrences of a pattern as one contiguous block of the sorted suffixes.

**Works because:** Suffixes starting with the pattern are consecutive in sorted order.
